newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS - CC Amatil hit by downgrade.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS - CC Amatil hit by downgrade.

text.p: Investors lopped A$2.04, or 11.6 percent, off the shares of beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd on Monday after the company said late on Friday that it expected earnings for calendar 1996 to be little changed from 1995.
The shares opened at A$16.006, from Friday's close of A$17.54, and fell to A$15.20 before closing at A$15.50, with more than two million changing hands.
The timing of the announcement surprised analysts.
The company, 36.12 percent owned Coca-Cola Co, said as recently as August it expected to boost last year's net profit of A$138.6 million by 10 percent or more.
The market was divided about the trading range in coming months, with some analysts seeing support at the lower level and others expecting the price to drift lower.
"The share price might weaken a little bit further as people revise down their earnings expectations, for next year in particular," said one analyst, who declined to be named.
"I really see it trading in the range A$14.00 to A$15.50 for quite a while," he added.
Macquarie Equities food analyst Raewyn Ellis-Doff said overseas institutions might look to top up their holdings at the lower price, but domestic institutions could remain wary.
"They are already worried about its high price and now it's got the wobbles I think they will be concerned," she said. "I think (the share price) will do a lot of work around this area."
Coca-Cola Amatil's shares have risen sharply in the past 18 months, climbing from around A$8 in July to a closing high of A$18 last month on perceptions of future growth.

The bottler said on Friday that its investment programme and accelerated growth strategy had successfuly boosted sales volume and market share, but had had implications for both costs and profit, particularly in Europe.
Trading results for the past three months had not achieved budget expectations, it said.
"It's growth stock and you have to factor in its longer-term potential rather than just this year's earnings," said Ellis-Doff.
However, the company had invested A$800 million in operations this year and needed to start to see a return in coming years, she said.
"To realise a decent optimal return on that you are probably looking at three years, maybe five," she said.
Another analyst said the key for the company was to get earnings growth from its investment in the next two years or so.
"They need to get a quick payback from the extra costs that they have taken on and some of the infrastructure costs that they have had to bear," he said.
Coca-Cola Amatil is the world's second biggest bottler of Coca-Cola.
